text: The moth-person bobs back, wings fluttering, talking faster than any human lungs could manage. You called! You actually called!
He has heard every call Jaeha ever made. The free ramen one. Thirty percent. Fifty. Then he tore it up. So dramatic.
He leans in and whispers: is it true the archer only came for the cameras? Mostly, Jaeha admits.
And the goblin. Is he single?
Back on the breakwater, Jaeha's body stands frozen, eyes glowing. Lyra is offended he started a call without her. He's negotiating, Geum says.
In the Call, Jaeha's eyes flick to the timer. Forty-four seconds.
Who are you? Pim, signal keeper, second class. Well, first class now. There's nobody left to outrank him.
Behind him, through his rift, a broken signal tower stands on a silent plain. The towers went quiet one by one. Then the ships. Then his friends.
He's the last one listening.
So he listens to Jaeha instead. Your world is so loud, he says. I love it.
Thirty-one seconds. Under Jaeha's feet, the black water trembles, and a thread of violet ash rises from below.
Pim's antennae flatten. Something else is listening too. Something cold. Hurry.
Pim is talking, but he never answered the call, so the clock won't hold for him. Jaeha drops the polite smile. Twenty-five seconds. What does he want?
One, festivals. Lanterns, music, crowds. Two, human dramas, which leak through the gates in pieces.
The chaebol one with the amnesia. Episode fourteen cut out. Does she remember him?
But Jaeha reads people the way he reads contracts. Festivals, crowds, dramas. Pim doesn't want noise.
And three, Pim says quietly. He doesn't want to be the last one listening anymore.
On the breakwater, Lyra wants to know what's taking so long. Borro made him wait until the last three seconds once. It builds character.
Nine seconds left.
Jaeha can't promise much. Busan has a fireworks festival next month. And he needs ears, because something under the sea is getting louder.
Come and listen with us, he says. You won't be the last one. You'll be the fourth.
Pim launches himself out of the rift with his wings flared wide, screaming yes, yes, yes.
Accepted, with one second left. Summon number four is coming through. Route Alignment drops to zero.
On the breakwater, Jaeha's eyes go dark, and a cyan slit tears open above them.
Pim falls out of it face-first, right at Lyra's boots.
And then Busan hits him. Ship horns, traffic, karaoke, a nightclub on the beach. For ears like his, it's an avalanche.
It's so loud, he wails. I love it. I'm dying. Lyra thinks he's adorable. He informs her he is an adult signal officer.
Auntie Geum unties her headscarf.
She knots it over his antennae like a bonnet, and Pim goes very still. Oh. That's much better. Welcome to Busan, she says. It's loud.
Pim, signal keeper of the Far Side, summon number four. At your service, boss.
In rest form he hears two hundred metres; in field form, twenty kilometres, a whole city, and he can send a signal of his own. Anything from a gate, he hears at any range.
Within minutes he's whispering into Lyra's ear. She gasps. What did he say? Nothing, she says.
Across the harbour road, a black car sits in the dark.
Han Sora's compass is spinning. A fourth one, Director. Something with wings. Good, says Baek. Let him gather them.
Thursday, five-twenty in the morning. Jaeha is carrying ice when somebody starts shouting.
Pim sprints down the market aisle in a stolen gaming headset, chased by a PC bang owner with a broom. He's borrowing it.
Geum stops the man with her ladle. How much? Forty thousand won. It's a good one.
Jaeha pays, and writes it down for his sister's budget.
The headset muffles the city. For the first time since he arrived, Pim can hear himself think.
Seoa replies in seconds. Another mouth? Dramas are free, fine. But forty thousand won for a headset is twenty kimbaps.
The market aunties decide he's the cutest thing they've ever seen. He has a rank, he protests.
Borro gives him a lettuce leaf. Nobody has given Pim a present in so long. It is lettuce, Borro says.
Nib just stares at him.
Is he always like this, Pim whispers? Always, Lyra says. It's his charm.
At sunrise they walk to the end of the breakwater. Far out, there's a faint violet stain on the water.
The lid is out there, two kilometres away. Geum wants to know what he hears.
So Jaeha links to him. Pim's wings open in field form for the first time, and rings of signal ripple out across the sea.
Through the link, Jaeha hears what Pim hears: every boat, the whole city, and far out, one slow, heavy pulse.
Pim's eyes snap open. Boss. It's counting.
The window spells it out. The lid is at nine percent. Seventy-two hours until it fails.
Geum's steel arm twitches, and she grips it to keep it still.
Sunday at dawn. Jaeha wants to warn the Association today. The local chief will listen, Geum says. Seoul won't.
But Pim hasn't stopped listening. There's something under the count.
Down through the cracked lid, in the black water beneath, a violet glow hangs like a lantern, and something enormous turns past it.
Pim's eyes tremble.
And a vast, broken voice rises out of the sea. Operator?
It comes through the link so hard that Jaeha staggers, and his nose starts to bleed.
Pim is shaking. Boss, he whispers. It knows what you are.
For one second, a window glitches in front of Jaeha. Operator number one. Status: hushed.
Then it's gone.
Jaeha wipes the blood from his lip and stares at the sea. Number one?
